Piper PA-32-301T

Smoke over Kingfisher

An instructor takes a very experienced pilot up to learn the Piper's newly installed autopilot. A fire in flight ends it. 2 people died.

Oklahoma City, 16 January 202312:14

Wheels up at Wiley Post

Two pilots take off from Wiley Post Airport for a lesson on the Piper's newly installed autopilot. Twenty-eight minutes later, the flight ends in a field near Kingfisher.

Your call

27 minutes after takeoff, the engine monitor, a panel display of engine data, shows oil pressure falling. It reads zero 12 seconds later.

No oil pressure, high above Oklahoma. What would you do?

{{ o.t }}
Show what happened
Words on this page
engine monitor a cockpit instrument that shows and stores engine readings such as temperatures and fuel flow during flight
oil pressure the pressure that pushes oil through an engine to lubricate it; at zero the moving parts are no longer properly oiled
ADS-B a system in which an aircraft keeps broadcasting its satellite position, altitude and speed, so its path can be followed and replayed
Next

What really happened

The report does not say what the crew saw or decided. ADS-B shows a descent starting about 12:41.

Got it

2 of 5
The last minutes12:42

Black smoke, then the dive

Witnesses see the Piper trailing black smoke. It rolls over and dives into the ground. A phone video shows the smoke and an explosion after impact.

Near Kingfisher

Nose first into a field

The plane hits a firm, level field almost straight down. The pilot and the instructor are killed. Fire burns in the air and on the ground and consumes almost the whole fuselage ahead of the tail.

What do the oil streaks tell investigators?

{{ o.t }}
{{ verdict }}

The streaks run opposite the direction of flight. The NTSB says that fits a significant oil leak in the air.

In the lab

A burned box remembers

The engine monitor arrives burned and no longer works. Its memory chip goes into a working lab unit, and the data downloads normally. It holds an engine reading every 6 seconds.

pages.tpl:
3 of 5
Clue 2 of 3

The oil suction screen holds debris. The sump holds a magneto drive cushion.

What is the debris made of?

{{ o.t }}
{{ verdict }}

Infrared matches it to the cushion's rubber, yet the cushion is undamaged. It is the only engine finding, never tied to the leak.

Words on this page
oil suction screen a mesh filter where the oil pump draws oil out of the sump, catching loose pieces
oil sump the reservoir at the bottom of a piston engine that holds its oil
magneto an engine driven generator that makes the sparks for a piston engine's spark plugs, independent of the aircraft's battery
magneto drive cushion a rubber coupling between the engine and the magneto that softens the jolts as the engine drives it
infrared test a lab method that identifies a material by measuring which wavelengths of infrared light it absorbs
Next

3 of 5
Clue 3 of 3

Less than half a quart of oil drains from the engine. Nothing in the core engine is breached in a way that explains the loss.

Where did the oil get out?

{{ o.t }}
{{ verdict }}

Impact and fire damage were too great to check the rest of the oil system. The exact source of the leak was never found.

Next chapter

4 of 5
The cause

The probable cause

Oil leaks from an unknown spot, the engine bay catches fire in flight, and control of the plane is lost.
Also found
  • Tests on the instructor find several drugs that are not approved for pilots or that are generally used for disqualifying conditions.
  • The report says the nature of the accident and a second qualified pilot on board suggest the drugs had no bearing on the outcome.

Lessons

What it teaches

  1. 1Oil streaks on a tail can show what happened in the air, even when the engine bay has burned.
  2. 2The memory chip of a burned engine monitor still held the last minutes of the flight.
  3. 3No single clue told the whole story. The video, oil streaks and engine data all fit an oil-fed fire.
